title: Ordinary open tensor balancing respects normalized coefficient composition
statement: Fix a prime l and finite extensions E,F,L of Q_l with algebra embeddings i:E→F and j:F→L. On the small pro-etale sites, use the constant integral coefficient data and scalar adjunctions of [def-pur-constant-scalar-tower-adjunction] and the open extension functors of [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. Let g:Z→W be any open immersion and M any ordinary sheaf of O_E-modules on Z. Write b_i for ordinaryBaseOpenTensor, the inverse scalar mate of the open restriction comparison [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate], and alpha_V for the left-adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism from successive ordinary scalar extension i,j to scalar extension j∘i, transferred along the identity-on-sections scalar restriction compositor. Then alpha_W(j_!^E M) followed by b_(j∘i)(M) equals scalar extension j at W of b_i(M), followed by b_j(C_i M), followed by j_!^L of alpha_Z(M). This is an equality of ordinary sheaf morphisms, without tower diagrams, derived categories, compactification, or finite-Tor hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; extension-by-zero presheaf in lemma-extension-by-zero; agent auxiliary Step 4 of lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-composition. The normalized adjunction associator is as in Stacks 07A6.

proof.text: Use ordinaryCoefficientComp, the proved ordinary-ring helper of lem-sp-proetale-open-scalar-cocycle, for the integral inclusion homomorphisms. It proves the restriction/pullback square composition with inverse restriction associators, without finite or torsion hypotheses. Cancel the inverse associators using the forward isomorphisms to obtain the forward normalized restriction cocycle.

The scalar mate defining ordinaryBaseOpenTensor is itself the inverse mate of the geometric restriction square. Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm therefore identifies its inverse with the left conjugate of the restriction/pullback isomorphism. Apply the conjugate equivalence to obtain the precise normalization at each of the three coefficient maps.

Expand leftAdjointUniq and ofNatIsoRight: the displayed ordinary associator is leftAdjointCompIso, whose inverse conjugates to the specified restriction compositor. The proved generic normalizedCocycle helper of lem-sp-proetale-open-scalar-cocycle now applies to the forward right cocycle and these five conjugate identifications. Its conclusion is exactly the ordinary open tensor composition formula.

theorem ordinaryBaseOpenTensor_composition
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra ℚ_[l] F] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] F]
    (i : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] F)
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[l] L] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] L]
    (j : F →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] L) {Z W : Scheme.{u}} (g : Z ⟶ W) [IsOpenImmersion g]
    (M : pbcModules Z ((constants l E).ring Z)) :
    let α (V : Scheme.{u}) :=
      (((pbcScalarAdjunction (constantMap l E F i V)).comp
          (pbcScalarAdjunction (constantMap l F L j V))).ofNatIsoRight
        (pbcRestrictComp _ _ _ (by
          unfold constantMap
          rw [← Functor.map_comp]
          congr 1))).leftAdjointUniq
            (pbcScalarAdjunction (constantMap l E L (j.comp i) V))
    (α W).hom.app ((PurCompactSupport.openExtension (constants l E) g).obj M) ≫
        (ordinaryBaseOpenTensor (change l E L (j.comp i)) g).app M =
      (pbcExtend (constantMap l F L j W)).map
          ((ordinaryBaseOpenTensor (change l E F i) g).app M) ≫
        (ordinaryBaseOpenTensor (change l F L j) g).app
          ((pbcExtend (constantMap l E F i Z)).obj M) ≫
        (PurCompactSupport.openExtension (constants l L) g).map ((α Z).hom.app M)
